models.purpose: Choose an evacuation route per area by an ant colony rule whose probability flips once a passage gets too crowded
models.summary: The floor plan becomes a mesh G(N, R, tau_0): nodes are stairs, exhibition rooms and entrances, routes are stairs, corridors and passages, tau_0 is the initial pheromone. The textbook probability (1) sends ant k from i to j in proportion to tau^alpha eta^beta. The paper argues that positive feedback would pack the shortest passage, so it adds a threshold. The human-chain length (2) is L_d = (S_T d + (S_T - 1) e) / n_d. The threshold is the time t_1 for that chain to clear, and the pheromone at the threshold is n v t_1. Below the threshold the probability keeps the textbook form; above it the probability is one minus that form (3), so a crowded passage is avoided. The resulting routes are drawn as orange arrows on the floor plan.

models.purpose: Compute the clearance time as the minimum over stairs of the maximum last-person time, with a blockage delay
models.summary: The human chain at stair i on floor j is L_ij = (S_ij d + (S_ij - 1) e) / n_f (4). The time down that stair is the sum of five pieces: walk to the stair, the stair itself, the chain at the exit, the walk to the door, and a blockage delay (5). Clearance is T = min { max t_i } (6). The delay (7) sums, over the floors that share the stair, the leftover chain length of the floor below divided by speed, and a switch beta is 1 when the delay is positive and 0 otherwise. Three floors reduce to two by treating the ground-floor flow as equivalent to a top-floor flow (9, 10), and the three basement exits merge into one because their channels have equal length. The reported clearance is T_min = max{T_3, T_5} + t_0 (16) with t_0 = 10 s, giving T_3 = 417.2 s and T_5 = 281.8 s at 10380 visitors.

models.purpose: Route responders to a room on a graph whose stair weights grow by the time that stair stays blocked
models.summary: The building is a graph G(N, R(t)) and the responders are a moving node. A stair's weight is the time to cross it at 2 m/s, plus the time until it is empty if visitors are still on it. The time of a route is T_i = sum_j t_ij + sum_j Delta t_ij (17), where t_ij is the aisle time and Delta t_ij is the stair time including congestion. For an emergency in room 101 on -1F and entry near stair B3, two routes are compared at four start times. Route A takes 130 s and route B 160 s when both are clear. At T = 90 both are blocked and B wins (180 s against 212 s); at T = 150 A wins (152 s against 160 s). The paper reads the switch off these cases and sets the threshold at T = 141.
